# tinymold

> tinymold is a content-addressed build cache for Rust. It runs as cargo's
> `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, keys every rustc and clippy-driver call by the content of
> its inputs, and restores outputs from a local store (reflink or hardlink)
> or a shared REAPI server. A warm cache serves `cargo build`, `cargo clippy`,
> `cargo test` builds and `cargo llvm-cov` builds without recompiling. It is
> pre-1.0: use it for development, tests, lints and coverage, not for the
> release builds you ship.

This file tells a coding agent how to add tinymold to a project: on a
developer machine, in GitHub Actions, on self-hosted runners, and on any
other CI system. Every step below is a shell command or a YAML snippet you
can apply as written. When a step and the linked docs disagree, the docs in
the repository win.

## What tinymold caches, and what it does not

- Cached: every rustc invocation cargo makes (dependencies, workspace
  crates, build scripts, proc-macros, binaries, test executables), including
  incremental builds and the instrumented compiles of `cargo llvm-cov`.
- Cached: `clippy-driver` calls under `cargo clippy`, with their lints
  replayed on a hit.
- Not cached: running tests. `cargo test` still executes every test; only
  its build is served from the cache.
- Not cached: C/C++ compiled by build scripts (`cc`, `cmake`). Build scripts
  re-run in an empty `target/`.
- A binary that links an edited crate is relinked in full. Unchanged
  binaries and test executables are restored without linking.
- tinymold replaces any other `RUSTC_WRAPPER` (sccache included). Use one or
  the other, not both.

## Rules for agents

1. Do not wire tinymold into release or publishing builds. Use it for
   development builds, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo llvm-cov`.
2. Never commit `TINYMOLD_REMOTE_AUTH` or any credential. Pass it from a CI
   secret.
3. Keep the store on the same filesystem as the checkouts. That is what
   makes a hit a reflink or hardlink instead of a byte copy.
4. Verify the integration (see "Verify it works") before reporting it done.
   A 0% hit rate on the second run means the setup is wrong.
5. Do not set `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` to a temporary directory to "isolate" a
   build. The store is what is shared; `target/` can stay where it is.

## Install

```sh
cargo install tinymold          # from crates.io
tinymold --version
tinymold doctor                 # host, toolchain, store, fast linkers on PATH
```

Prebuilt binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows on x86_64 and ARM64, with a
`SHA256SUMS` file, are attached to every release:
https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinymold/releases. Asset names are
`tinymold-<version>-<target>.tar.gz` (`.zip` on Windows), where `<target>`
is a Rust target triple such as `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` or
`aarch64-apple-darwin`.

## On a developer machine or an agent sandbox

Set the wrapper once, for every cargo invocation, in the user's cargo
config (`~/.cargo/config.toml`) or the project's `.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[build]
rustc-wrapper = "tinymold"
```

Or per shell:

```sh
export RUSTC_WRAPPER=tinymold
cargo build && cargo clippy --all-targets && cargo test
```

Worktrees, branch switches and agent sandboxes on one machine share a single
store, so a second checkout of the same commit builds from the cache. Two
optional commands make worktrees start warm:

```sh
tinymold snapshot save              # after building, in the source worktree
tinymold snapshot restore           # in a new worktree, before cargo build
tinymold fresh restore              # after a checkout or rebase, undo mtime-only changes
```

Keep the store bounded:

```sh
tinymold gc --max-age 14d --max-size 20G
```

The wrapper also collects garbage in the background; set
`TINYMOLD_AUTO_GC=0` to turn that off.

## GitHub Actions (hosted runners)

Add two steps around the existing cargo commands. The store travels in
GitHub's own cache; no server is needed.

```yaml
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy
      - uses: tinyhumansai/tinymold@v0          # install, RUSTC_WRAPPER, restore the store
      - run: cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
      - run: cargo test --all-features
      - uses: tinyhumansai/tinymold/save@v0     # push, hit-rate summary, gc, save
        if: always()
```

Coverage works the same way; install cargo-llvm-cov before it:

```yaml
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: cargo llvm-cov --workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info
```

Placement rules:

- The setup step goes after the Rust toolchain step and before the first
  cargo command. The save step is the last step, with `if: always()`.
- Use one setup/save pair per job. Jobs that build different things (say,
  a Linux and a macOS job, or a feature matrix) need a distinct `cache-key`
  so their stores do not overwrite each other:

  ```yaml
      - uses: tinyhumansai/tinymold@v0
        with:
          cache-key: ${{ matrix.features }}
  ```

- Remove any `Swatinem/rust-cache` or `actions/cache` step that caches
  `target/`, and any `RUSTC_WRAPPER: sccache` / `mozilla-actions/sccache-action`
  step. They duplicate or fight tinymold's cache.
- `v0` moves to the newest 0.x release. Pin a full tag such as `v0.0.1` to
  stay put.

Setup inputs (`tinyhumansai/tinymold@v0`):

| Input | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | `latest` | Release tag to install |
| `install` | `release` | `release` (download and check SHA256SUMS), `source` (cargo install from `source-path`), `none` (tinymold already on PATH) |
| `backend` | `github` | `github`, `remote`, `both`, or `none` (a persistent local store) |
| `store` | `~/.cache/tinymold` | Store directory |
| `cache-key` | `''` | Extra text in the GitHub cache key |
| `remote-url` | `''` | `grpc://host:port` or `grpcs://host[:port]` |
| `remote-auth` | `''` | `user:password`, from a secret |
| `remote-instance` | `''` | REAPI instance name |

Save inputs (`tinyhumansai/tinymold/save@v0`): `max-age` (default `7d`),
`max-size` (default `4G`), `push` (`auto`, `true`, `false`), `save-cache`
(default `true`).

The setup step exports `RUSTC_WRAPPER=tinymold`, `TINYMOLD_STORE`,
`TINYMOLD_LOG`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` and, with a remote, the
`TINYMOLD_REMOTE_*` variables. The save step writes the hit rate to the job
summary.

## Self-hosted GitHub runners

A self-hosted runner keeps its disk between jobs, so skip GitHub's cache and
use a persistent store that every runner on the machine shares (the store is
safe for concurrent use):

```yaml
      - uses: tinyhumansai/tinymold@v0
        with:
          backend: none
          store: /var/cache/tinymold
      # ... cargo commands ...
      - uses: tinyhumansai/tinymold/save@v0       # still runs gc, so the store stays bounded
        if: always()
```

To share one cache across machines, add a remote server and use
`backend: remote` (or `both` to keep GitHub's cache as well).

## Other CI systems (GitLab, Buildkite, Jenkins, CircleCI, custom runners)

There is no plugin; the integration is environment variables plus caching
one directory. The recipe, in any CI:

1. Install the binary before the first cargo command (cache it, or download
   a release asset and check it against `SHA256SUMS`).
2. Export the environment:

   ```sh
   export RUSTC_WRAPPER=tinymold
   export TINYMOLD_STORE="$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.tinymold"   # any path your CI can cache
   export TINYMOLD_LOG="$TINYMOLD_STORE/../tinymold.log"
   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0
   export TINYMOLD_SAVE_START="$(date +%s)"
   ```

3. Restore `$TINYMOLD_STORE` from the CI system's cache. Key it on the OS,
   the architecture, `rustc -vV` and the hash of `Cargo.lock`, and fall back
   to less specific keys: any recent store helps, because entries are keyed
   by content, never by path or time.
4. Run the cargo commands as usual.
5. At the end of the job, whether or not it passed:

   ```sh
   tinymold stats --markdown                                 # hit rate, for the job log
   tinymold gc --max-age 7d --max-size 4G --grace 0s         # bound the store before saving it
   tinymold remote push --since "$TINYMOLD_SAVE_START"       # only with a remote server
   ```

6. Save `$TINYMOLD_STORE` to the CI cache.

GitLab CI, for example:

```yaml
test:
  image: rust:latest
  variables:
    RUSTC_WRAPPER: tinymold
    TINYMOLD_STORE: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/.tinymold
    TINYMOLD_LOG: $CI_PROJECT_DIR/tinymold.log
    CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  cache:
    key:
      files: [Cargo.lock]
      prefix: tinymold-$CI_RUNNER_EXECUTABLE_ARCH
    paths: [.tinymold/]
  before_script:
    - cargo install --locked tinymold
  script:
    - cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
    - cargo test
  after_script:
    - tinymold stats --log tinymold.log
    - tinymold --store .tinymold gc --max-age 7d --max-size 4G --grace 0s
```

`cargo install` itself runs with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=tinymold` in that job, before
tinymold exists; run it with `env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER cargo install --locked tinymold`,
or download the release binary instead, when the variable is set globally.

Runners with a persistent disk (bare metal, long-lived VMs, a Kubernetes
node with a host path) need no CI cache at all: point `TINYMOLD_STORE` at a
directory on that disk and run `tinymold gc` at the end of each job or from
cron.

## A shared remote cache

For many repositories, runners or machines, run bazel-remote (or any REAPI
v2 cache) and point tinymold at it. On a local miss the wrapper asks the
server first; the job uploads what it built in one batch at the end.

```sh
export TINYMOLD_REMOTE_URL=grpcs://cache.example.com   # grpc://host:9092 without TLS
export TINYMOLD_REMOTE_AUTH=ci:password                # from a secret; omit for anonymous reads
tinymold remote check                                  # reachable, credential accepted
```

Give write credentials only to trusted CI (pushes to the default branch,
same-repository pull requests). Forks read anonymously. tinymold re-hashes
everything it fetches, so a remote can make a build miss but never restore
different bytes. Deployment files for Docker Compose and Kubernetes:
https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinymold/tree/main/deploy/bazel-remote

## Environment variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `RUSTC_WRAPPER=tinymold` | Turns the cache on for every cargo command |
| `TINYMOLD_STORE` | Store directory; default `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tinymold`, then `~/.cache/tinymold` |
| `TINYMOLD_LOG` | Append one `hit`/`miss` line per compile; read it with `tinymold stats` |
| `TINYMOLD_TRACE` | Write a Chrome trace event per wrapper step |
| `TINYMOLD_AUTO_GC` | `0` turns off background garbage collection |
| `TINYMOLD_REMOTE_URL` | REAPI server; unset means local only |
| `TINYMOLD_REMOTE_AUTH` | `user:password` for the server |
| `TINYMOLD_REMOTE_INSTANCE` | REAPI instance name |
| `TINYMOLD_REMOTE_TIMEOUT` | Per-call timeout such as `2s`; default `5s` |

## Verify it works

Build twice from an empty `target/` with the same store. The second run must
be mostly hits:

```sh
export RUSTC_WRAPPER=tinymold TINYMOLD_LOG=/tmp/tinymold.log
cargo build && rm -rf target && : > "$TINYMOLD_LOG"
cargo build
tinymold stats --min-hit-rate 90       # exits 1 below 90% hits
```

In CI, run the same check in a second job that restores the first job's
store, or read the hit-rate table the save step writes to the job summary.
If hits stay at zero:

- `tinymold doctor` shows the store the wrapper uses; make sure the restore
  and the build agree on it;
- another `RUSTC_WRAPPER` (sccache) or a `rustc-wrapper` in a
  `.cargo/config.toml` may be overriding tinymold;
- a different toolchain, `RUSTFLAGS` or feature set between runs changes the
  keys by design;
- coverage builds embed the checkout's absolute path, so instrumented
  workspace crates only hit at the same path (CI runners keep it fixed).

- [GitHub Actions spec](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinymold/blob/main/docs/specs/github-actions.md): inputs, cache keys, self-hosted runners
- [Remote cache spec](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinymold/blob/main/docs/specs/remote.md): the REAPI tier and its configuration
- [rustc wrapper spec](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinymold/blob/main/docs/specs/rustc-wrapper.md): what is cached and what passes through
- [Cache key spec](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinymold/blob/main/docs/specs/cache-key.md): what goes into a key, and what breaks reuse
- [Garbage collection spec](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinymold/blob/main/docs/specs/gc.md): `tinymold gc` and background collection
- [Benchmarks](https://github.com/tinyhumansai/tinymold/blob/main/bench/README.md): every number, the machine it came from, and how to reproduce it
